rules.title: New Jersey residential rental application fee cap ($50, CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted annually by CPI (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island, All Items) only if the percent change is greater than zero, with the Director of Consumer Affairs publishing the limit. Penalties up to $500 (first), $750 (second), $1,000 (subsequent), and the amount wrongfully charged is remitted to the applicant. The Director must adopt implementing rules, including a mechanism for reporting violations.
rules.key_value: $50 max application fee (CPI-adjusted annually); penalties up to $500 / $750 / $1,000 per offense; wrongfully charged amount remitted to applicant

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental properties other than dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings; licensees of the NJ Real Estate Commission are not covered unless they are the landlord.
coverage.other_conditions: Real estate licensees exempt unless the licensee is the landlord.

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent; licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission, unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.effective_date_note: Act takes effect on the first day of the fourth month next following enactment (approved January 20, 2026); computed in code. The Director may take anticipatory action beforehand.

effective_date_formula.verbatim: This act shall take effect on the first day of the fourth month next following the date of enactment

rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.review_note: The CPI adjustment starts January 1 of the year next following enactment, so the cap may be above $50 after the adjustment; the text does not state an adjusted figure.

result.doc_summary: P.L. 2025, c.405 (A4899), approved January 20, 2026, caps New Jersey residential rental application fees at $50 (CPI-adjusted annually), sets escalating civil penalties with refund to the applicant, exempts units in one- and two-family dwellings and non-landlord real estate licensees, directs the Division of Consumer Affairs to adopt rules, and takes effect the first day of the fourth month after enactment.
